text:
Evidence supports using observed user-specific intervals, but the searches found no direct empirical comparison establishing item-pair mean gaps as an equivalent substitute. [DeepTimeDelta](https://repository.tudelft.nl/record/uuid%3A34ffc4b0-6c61-4649-a628-9d1f7b9fa846) extends recurrent recommendation with actual interaction gaps and reports improvements, particularly after longer inactivity. [TUR](https://www.comp.hkbu.edu.hk/~lichen/download/Yongxin_WISE22.pdf) incorporates observed adjacent-event intervals and elapsed time to recommendation into GRU gates. These motivate temporal conditioning; they do not validate replacing individual intervals with population averages for item transitions.

An item-pair mean gap is a deterministic feature of transition identity once estimated. Therefore, gains could reflect transition encoding rather than sensitivity to a user's elapsed time; this is a methodological inference, not an established result from the retrieved papers. Recommended controls: identical GRUs with no temporal feature, actual historical gaps, pair-average gaps, transition-count features, and randomly assigned pair features matched in dimension. Shuffle observed gaps across fixed interaction positions while preserving item order; separately permute estimated mean gaps across pairs while retaining coverage and counts. Within-pair shuffling tests user-specific timing beyond pair identity where repeated transitions exist. [An Analysis of Sequential Recommendation Datasets](https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-2955/paper8.pdf) examines timestamp ambiguity and sequence shuffling, but sequence shuffling also changes transitions and cannot isolate timestamp information.

Sparse-coverage support remains unestablished for this proxy. Measure training-only pair counts, singleton fraction, and validation-history transition coverage; report performance for seen/unseen pairs and support bins. Fit means and fallback statistics exclusively on training interactions. Use only timestamps available in the observed prefix; target-event time must not enter next-item prediction unless explicitly supplied at inference.
